name: Windows Terminal
description: Basisset aan aanbevolen Windows 11-beveiligingsinstellingen voor Windows Terminal.

settings.name: Disable Sudo
settings.description: Disabling Sudo prevents the use of elevated privileges within Windows Terminal.
settings.rationale: Disabling Sudo may be necessary for security reasons, but it reduces the ability to perform administrative tasks within Windows Terminal.

settings.id: Prevent access to the command prompt
settings.name: Prevent access to the command prompt
settings.description: Preventing access to the command prompt restricts users from executing commands directly within Windows Terminal.
settings.rationale: Preventing access to the command prompt may be necessary for security reasons, but it reduces the ability to perform administrative tasks within Windows Terminal.

settings.id: Disable the command prompt script processing also?
settings.name: Disable the command prompt script processing also?
settings.description: Disabling the command prompt script processing restricts users from executing scripts directly within Windows Terminal.
settings.rationale: Disabling the command prompt script processing may be necessary for security reasons, but it reduces the ability to perform administrative tasks within Windows Terminal.

settings.name: Powershell script execution policy
settings.value: Allow local scripts and remote signed scripts
settings.description: Setting the Powershell script execution policy to Restricted prevents the execution of scripts within Windows Terminal.
settings.rationale: Restricting Powershell script execution enhances security by preventing potentially harmful scripts from running, but it may limit administrative automation tasks within Windows Terminal.

settings.name: Turn on Module Logging
settings.description: Turning on module logging helps track the activities of PowerShell modules for security and auditing purposes.
settings.rationale: Enabling module logging enhances security by providing detailed logs of PowerShell module activities, which can be useful for detecting and investigating suspicious behavior.

settings.id: Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging
settings.name: Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging
settings.description: Turning on PowerShell script block logging records the content of all executed script blocks for security and auditing purposes.
settings.rationale: Enabling script block logging enhances security by providing detailed logs of PowerShell script activities, which can be useful for detecting and investigating suspicious behavior.

settings.id: Log script block invocation start / stop events:
settings.name: Log script block invocation start / stop events
settings.description: Logging script block invocation start and stop events helps track the execution of PowerShell scripts for security and auditing purposes.
settings.rationale: Enabling this logging enhances security by providing detailed logs of when script blocks start and stop, which can be useful for detecting and investigating suspicious behavior.

settings.name: Turn on Script Execution
settings.description: Turning on script execution allows PowerShell scripts to run, which is necessary for automation and administrative tasks.
settings.rationale: Enabling script execution ensures that authorized scripts can run while maintaining control over the execution policy.

settings.id: Enable Windows Package Manager command line interfaces
settings.name: Enable Windows Package Manager command line interfaces
settings.description: Enabling Windows Package Manager command line interfaces allows the use of the Windows Package Manager for software installation and management.
settings.rationale: Enabling this setting facilitates software management and automation through the Windows Package Manager.

changelog.notes: Release of Windows Terminal Hardening baseline version 1.0.0
